chunks: He said: Abu Ghalib Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Zurari, may Allah have mercy on him, reported to me from my uncle Abul Hasan Ali ibn Sulaiman ibn al-Jahm, from Abu Abdillah Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Tayalisi, from al-Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim al-Thaqafi, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali, peace be upon them both,
about the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: "Then those, Allah will change their evil deeds into good deeds, and Allah is ever all-Forgiving, Merciful."

He, peace be upon him, said: "The believing sinner will be brought on the Day of Resurrection until he is made to stand at the station of Reckoning. Then Allah, the Most High, will take charge of his reckoning, not revealing his account to anyone. He will make him recognize his sins, until when he confesses his evil deeds, Allah says to the recorders: Change them into good deeds, and display them to the people. Then the people will say: Did this servant not have even a single evil deed?! Then Allah commands that he be sent to Paradise.
This is the interpretation of the verse, and it is specifically regarding the sinners among our Shia."

key_terms.الكتبة: The recorders, recording angels (Kiraman Katibin) who document human deeds
key_terms.تأويل: Interpretation, deeper meaning — esoteric exegesis of a Quranic verse
key_terms.حسنات: Good deeds, virtues — what sins will be converted into
key_terms.سيئات: Evil deeds, sins — moral transgressions that will be transformed
key_terms.يبدل: To change or transform — the divine act of converting sins into good deeds

ai.seo_question: How does Imam al-Baqir interpret the Quranic verse about Allah changing evil deeds into good deeds?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (AS) interprets Quran 25:70 to describe how Allah will personally handle the reckoning of believing sinners on the Day of Judgment, privately showing them their sins and then, after their confession, commanding the recording angels to transform those sins into good deeds. This hadith was narrated through Muhammad ibn Muslim al-Thaqafi, a close companion of both Imam al-Baqir and Imam al-Sadiq, and it reflects the Shia understanding of divine mercy extended specifically to faithful believers who committed sins.
